title: Brazil Banned Everyone From This Island. The Reason Lives in the Trees

scenes.text: No one is allowed on this island. By law.
Ilha da Queimada Grande, about 30 kilometres off the coast of Brazil. 43 hectares of forest and a lighthouse that nobody mans.
Around 11,000 years ago, rising seas cut it off from the mainland, trapping a population of pit vipers with almost nothing to eat on the ground.
So they went up. The golden lancehead hunts migrating birds from the branches, with venom about five times more potent than its mainland cousin's.
Locals say one snake per square metre. Scientists estimate around 2,000 golden lanceheads, found nowhere else on Earth.
The Brazilian Navy keeps the island closed; only researchers with permits get in. The snakes keep the trees.

description:
Ilha da Queimada Grande, about 30 kilometres off Brazil, is closed to the public by the Brazilian Navy because of the golden lancehead, a pit viper found nowhere else, with venom around five times more potent than its mainland relative.
Cut off by rising seas about 11,000 years ago, the snakes adapted to hunting migrating birds from the trees; estimates put their number at around 2,000.
Would you set foot on Snake Island with a permit?

first_comment: Legend says the last lighthouse keeper's family was attacked by snakes coming in through the windows, but there is no record it happened. Which forbidden place should we cover next?
